newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard has outlined the ground rules for assessing changes to the taxation system by linking reform to the provision of increased economic benefits for voters. Howard says any tax reform changes must generate employment, boost exportsand lead to higher living standards. Page 1.

The government's plans to allow Australia's large "super" unions to be split up may be compromised by a serious flaw in the drafting of the Workplace Relations Act. Several labour law experts believe the act's new provisions designed to open the way for the break-up of the large amalgamated unions formed in recent years will be ineffective because of the drafting of a key clause. Page 3.

The final plank of the government's industrial relations reforms came into effect yesterday when the Industrial Relations Court of Australia's jurisdiction was transferred to the Federal Court. Page 3.

The Construction Forestry Mining and Energy Union has vowed to lead a "tough fight" against the push to privatise the New South Wales electricity industry unveiled last week by the NSW Treasurer and Energy Minister, Michael Egan. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard is set to reject Aboriginal people's focus on native title and stolen children today and seek "practical action" on health and education. Howard will warn Aboriginal leaders to concentrate on practical improvements to lifestyle and job prospects of their people instead of areas that could result in community division. Page 1.

Independent Yvonne Moran scored an eight percentage point swing against the sitting Liberal candidate and won almost 16 percent of the vote in a Labour by-election victory in Kurwongbah, north of Brisbane. Moran issued how-to-vote cards headed "One Nation, Our Nation", but denied she was linked to Pauline Hanson's One Nation Party. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello says the government expects banks to pass on a 0.5 percent cut in interest rates, rather than a reduced 0.35 point cut which went through on Friday. The government has threatened punishment if the four major banks fail to justify their decision to allow home loan borrowers the full percentage reduction. Page 1.

Police have followed up on a possible lead that kidnap victim Kerry Whelan could be held in a mine shaft by searching a farm in the NSW Southern Highlands. Police would not confirm whether the farm was owned by a former employee of Crown Equipment, where Whelan's husband Bernard is a senior executive, but it is believed there are no new clues into the disappearance. Page 3.

Former Liberal leader John Hewson has called on Prime Minister John Howard to continue in his push to put tax reform on the political agenda as well as boost immigration, accelerate industrial relations reform and cut tariffs without demanding any trade-offs from Australia's trading partners. Page 2.

The Transport Workers Union is studying the tactics of their trucking counterparts in France, who successfully brought the country's transport industry to a standstill last year. Officials are looking for ways to improve their bargaining position when they launch two major two-year claims against employers this week. Page 2.

Chinese Vice Premier Zhu Rongji has told a business dinner in Perth that the race debate currently sweeping Australia is not hurting business relations between the two countries. After a whirlwind tour of Perth and Adelaide, Zhu travels to Canberra today to meet with Prime Minister John Howard and senior Government Ministers. Page 2.

A new survey to be released today by the Judicial Commission of New South Wales is expected to find child sexual assault is being prosecuted more rigorously and punished more severely than in recent years. The report has found child sex offenders are more likely to be male, aged around 40, and abuse mainly girls in their own family. Page 3.

A new international economic survey has found Australia ranked 10th among 115 nations in terms of economic freedom. The survey, entitled the Economic Freedom of the World Report, was measured in terms of finance markets, the size of the public sector, the magnitude of the tax burden and restraints in international trade. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A review of the tax system, including the goods and services tax, will be discussed this week in Federal Cabinet as the government prepares for major reform in its second term. Ministers believe the tax would be politically risky, but essential for the government to be seen by voters as being strong on new tax reform. Page 1.

Investigations into the abduction of Kerry Whelan have focused on a property in the Southern Highlands belonging to a former employee of the company in which her husband is a senior executive. Police say nothing significant has been discovered, and they are likely to search other properties during the investigation. Page 1.

Telstra is expected to make a submission to Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston next month to impose a new 50 cent fee to calls for 013 directory assistance. Prime Minister John Howard has previously indicated he had difficulties with the plan and Telstra executives were told to consult further with community groups. Page 3.

The NSW Health Department says there is no evidence the Ross River Virus is gaining a foothold in Sydney despite 45 suspected cases in the west of the city reported between January and April this year. The outbreak is expected to lessen due to the inactivity of mosquitoes, which transmit the virus, in colder months. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Federal Government has dismissed calls for an apology to Aboriginal people "stolen" from their families, and has announced a review of ATSIC and Aboriginal legal services. The Reconciliation Convention commences today, with Prime Minister John Howard set to address the convention this morning. Page 1.

The first real test of the Family Law Reform Act will come today, with a verdict expected on a case involving a woman seeking to move her daughters interstate. Attorney-General Daryl Williams will seek to keep the woman near her husband, and further the Act's aims to promote shared parenting after divorce. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
